one_liner: Sherlock (sherlock-project) is a local open-source Python CLI for username enumeration across 400+ sites. It has no hosted HTTP API or credentials, so it can't become a standard hosted-API toolkit.
auth_notes: The CLI help on the repo page lists no credential or API key options. It runs locally and writes results to local files. Other products named Sherlock (shebang's auth service, Aleph Alpha's Pharia Data Sherlock, the .NET assembly MCP, the Dart/Flutter profiling MCP) are unrelated to sherlock-project.
access_notes: The MIT-licensed CLI is free to install (pipx, docker, dnf) and run locally. There is no vendor-hosted service to get credentials for.
blocker_notes: It is a local CLI with no hosted API. A toolkit would have to shell out to the CLI. None of the provided pages confirm any MCP server for sherlock-project. The Burnsedia community MCP URL comes from the draft and is not in the provided pages. The registry entry com.hostsherlock/mcp is also unconfirmed and may belong to a different product. The mcp field is kept as community with low confidence.

evidence.quote: Hunt down social media accounts by username across [400+ social networks](https://sherlockproject.xyz/sites)
| `pipx install sherlock-project` | `pip` or [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) may be used in place of `pipx` |
Accounts found will be stored in an individual text file with the corresponding username (e.g `user123.txt`).
